production_example.old_outcome: terminal timing failure because M5 required 2/3 samples even though one exact real MP3 was already valid

problem.root_cause: M5 synthesized and measured real TTS audio but discarded it. M6 then synthesized the same narration again, so stochastic Chirp duration made M5 timing prediction unreliable.

architecture.principle: A real TTS file that passes the final duration gate is the artifact to preserve. Do not predict a future synthesis when the accepted synthesis already exists.
m5: still observes three real syntheses on the stability path
selects the closest actual MP3 inside the same final M6 tolerance
stores the exact accepted MP3 under /data/voiceover-candidates/<job>/accepted.mp3
registers candidate SHA/duration/audio metadata and the exact committed M5 provider-usage ledger before storyboard commit
database: register_voiceover_candidate validates exact active script run, narration, voice/locale/sku, committed M5 timing-probe usage, path and final duration tolerance
begin_voiceover_v2 adopts a matching candidate and reuses its committed M5 usage ledger instead of reserving new M6 TTS usage
legacy M6 synthesis path remains only when no candidate exists
m6: begin_voiceover_v2 returns reuse_candidate plus immutable candidate metadata
reuse branch promotes the staged MP3 to /data/voiceovers/<job>/final.mp3
promotion requires exact SHA and duration
normalizer requires exact bytes/duration/sample-rate/channels/codec from DB candidate metadata
then existing complete_voiceover final gate persists the exact reused file
media_worker: promotion uses a hard link and re-verifies SHA and ffprobe metadata

db_transaction_test.method: apply migration + synthetic candidate registration + begin_voiceover_v2 adoption inside one transaction, then ROLLBACK

next_step: Commit/push, apply DB migration, deploy media worker, publish only M5 and M6, verify exact live state, then one fresh PL15.
